purpose: Control-level evaluation model for GDPR-oriented public, authenticated-app, repo, document, and cloud audits. It limits audit conclusions to controls with applicable scope and available evidence.

evidence_tiers.tier_1_automated: Observed or tested by scanner, crawler, repo analysis, app flow, cloud/IaC analysis, or schema validation.
evidence_tiers.tier_3_document: Parsed uploaded document or structured sample, labelled confirmed-from-document when extraction is reliable.
evidence_tiers.human_review: Privacy/legal reviewer decision; required for legal basis, proportionality, transfers, AI/high-risk, DPIA necessity, and non-enforceable controls.

coverage_rules: Coverage is computed from applicable controls, assessed controls, and evidence tiers used.
Do not use unvalidated percentage claims in reports.
A control is not_applicable only after applies_if has been evaluated.
Missing evidence results in unknown, not pass.
Non-enforceable controls never produce pass/fail without human review.
High-risk unknown is defined as result == unknown and severity_if_failed in {high, critical}.
Any high-risk unknown blocks clean summary output.
A6 routing is catalogue-authoritative: only decision_flags.routes_to_legal_review_if_triggered == true routes a control to the legal review packet.

staleness_policy.stale_warning_template: This audit uses GDPR framework v{framework_version}, last reviewed on {framework_last_reviewed}. Please verify that no material changes in EDPB guidance, CJEU case law, national overlays, or transfer rules affect this report before relying on it.

examples: European Commission data-protection legal framework pages
Official national legal texts such as TDDDG
CJEU GDPR judgments affecting data subject rights, Art.82, transfers, definitions, EDPB decisions
national DPA guidance when jurisdiction is active

source_registry.title: EDPB guidance, recommendations, opinions, coordinated enforcement framework, and templates
ICO PECR storage and access technologies guidance

changes: Added normative source hierarchy and mandatory review triggers.
Added framework-level and control-level staleness metadata.
Added staleness output policy with warning and degraded modes.
Added source registry and framework changelog fields.
Renamed Germany overlay terminology to TDDDG and retained tdddg-de overlay key.

in_scope: EDPB guidance, recommendations, opinions, CEF outputs, templates and tools directly relevant to GDPR
CJEU case law directly interpreting GDPR
direct ePrivacy-style privacy overlays including UK PECR and Germany TDDDG
out_of_scope: general cybersecurity/product-safety/digital-market regimes unless independently grounded in GDPR or a direct privacy overlay
scope_restriction.rule: Adjacent regimes may be context only. They must not create controls, findings, severity ratings, or compliance conclusions inside this GDPR catalogue.

source_registry_scope: GDPR and directly related privacy overlays only; excludes NIS2, AI Act, CRA, and adjacent regimes.

stage-early.notes: Reduced profile for critical, broadly applicable controls. Self-reported evidence is allowed but visibly labelled.

stage-growth.notes: Broad coverage with some enterprise governance, transfer, and advanced AI controls deferred.

stage-enterprise.notes: Full catalogue and full legal-review packet.

role_profile_model.engineer: Implementation-focused output. Shows concrete remediation, evidence, and test hints.
role_profile_model.product: Risk, ownership, priority, and next-action output. Hides raw control mechanics by default.
role_profile_model.dpo: Obligation, evidence, limitation, and legal-source output.
role_profile_model.counsel: Facts, legal sources, and precise legal questions only. No automated legal conclusions.

decision_layer_model.high_risk_unknown_definition: result == unknown AND severity_if_failed in {high, critical}

applicability_model.evaluation_rule: Evaluate applies_if before evidence collection; false returns not_applicable; missing required variable returns unknown_applicability and the control is not evaluated.
